title: Quantification of Mouse Heart Left Ventricular Function, Myocardial Strain, and Hemodynamic Forces by Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Imaging
protocol: Prepare the mouse cradle with the temperature set to 40 °C.
Turn on the ECG/respiratory interface module and battery setup.
Start the software for real-time monitoring of ECG and respiratory signals.
Measure body weight of the mouse.
Place the mouse in an anesthesia induction chamber under a fume hood extraction arm.
Provide 3-4% isoflurane in a mixture of 0.2 L/min O2 and 0.2 L/min medical air.
Apply a small drop of eye ointment to each eye when the animal is fully anesthetized.
Close the eyelids of the mouse.
Place the mouse in the supine position on the mouse cradle.
Hook the incisors of the mouse in the bite bar on the mouse cradle.
Adjust the nose cone to fit properly.
Visually check if the breathing is stable below 100 breaths/min.
Move the mouse cradle so that the heart is centered in the RF coil and magnet iso-center.
Use petroleum jelly to insert the rectal temperature probe.
Tape the fiber-optic cable of the temperature probe to the mouse cradle.
Place the respiratory balloon on the lower abdomen of the mouse and secure it with tape.
Insert two ECG electrode needles subcutaneously in the thorax at the height of the forepaws, taping them down gently.
Check respiration and ECG signals for quality and correct trigger points detection by software.
Ensure respiratory rate is 50-80 breaths/min, heart rate ~400-600 beats/min, and body temperature around 37 °C.
Adjust isoflurane administration if the respiratory rate is outside of the range.
Reduce the temperature of the animal heating system if body temperature exceeds 37 °C.
Place the RF coil over the mouse.
Reconnect ECG electrodes and respiratory balloon plugs to the ECG/respiratory interface module as necessary.
Check stability of the ECG signal after placing the cradle in the magnet bore.
Reposition the ECG electrodes for a better signal if needed, ensuring it does not change animal orientation significantly.
Adjust ECG and respiratory gating parameters within the signal monitoring software.
Set trigger points at R-peaks during the flat portion of the respiratory signal.
Define a blanking period that is 10-15 ms shorter than the R-R interval.
Perform center frequency calibration.
Conduct an un gated SCOUT scan with zero offset to determine mouse position.
Adjust cradle position if heart is not within 0.5-1 cm of FOV center.
Redo SCOUT scan after adjusting cradle position.
Perform a manual shim and RF calibration using vendor methods.
Based on initial SCOUT, perform a gated single-frame GRE scout scan.
Use 5 slices in 3 orthogonal directions to locate exact heart position.
Perform a gated single-frame multi-slice SA scout scan.
Use the previous GRE scout to position 4-5 slices in a mid-left ventricular position, perpendicular to the long axis of the heart.
Adjust the number of cardiac frames (Nframes) such that Nframes × TR is ~60-70% of the R-R interval.
Perform a gated single-slice GRE scan to generate the long-axis 2-chamber (2CH) scout.
Position a slice perpendicular to the previous SA views running parallel to the connection points between the left and right ventricle.
Move this slice to the middle of the left ventricle.
Check in the coronal image of the GRE scout if the slice is aligned with the LV long axis through the apex.
Perform another gated single-slice GRE scan to generate the 4-chamber scout scan.
Position a slice perpendicular to the 2CH scout scan.
Align the slice to the center of the long axis, passing through the mitral valve and the apex.
Adjust the slice in the SA views to be parallel to the posterior and anterior ventricular wall.
Place the slice between the two papillary muscles.
Ensure the slice remains centered within the ventricle throughout the cardiac cycle.
Perform a gated sequential multi-slice SA GRE scan for systolic function measurements.
Position a midventricular slice perpendicular to the LV long axis in both 2CH and 4CH views.
Center the slice in the heart and increase the number of slices (typically odd, e.g., 7 or 9) without gaps from base to apex.
Perform three sequential single-slice retrospectively gated GRE scans in the midventricular SA view.
Perform a single-slice GRE scan in the 2CH view.
Perform a single-slice GRE scan in the 4CH view.
Optimize the final 2CH and 4CH slice orientations based on multi-slice SA views and available scout scans.
Perform an additional retrospectively gated single-slice GRE scan in a 3CH view.
Position the 3CH slice perpendicular to the midventricular SA view, similar to the position of the long-axis 4CH view.
Turn the 3CH slice 45° to pass from the anterior wall to the papillary muscle closest to the posterior wall.
Inspect the basal SA slice to ensure it passes through the mitral and aortic valve.
Inspect the final long-axis 4CH view to confirm that the slice goes through the apex.
Remove the mouse from the cradle after detaching all other measurement equipment.
Turn off the anesthesia.
In the case of longitudinal experiments, place the mouse in a pre-warmed housing cage at 37 °C for recovery until the animal is awake and active.
Clean all equipment that has been used with cleaning wipes or 70% alcohol.
Generate Digital Imaging and Communication in Medicine (DICOM) files for the prospectively gated MRI data.
Copy DICOM files together with MRI raw data files of retrospectively gated scans to a secure server.
Open reconstruction software Retrospective.
Load raw data file corresponding to a retrospectively gated MRI scan.
Inspect Raw navigator signal.
Flip signal if peaks are registered upside down using up/down switch.
Manually adjust heart rate values if automated detection does not correspond to 10% observed values during each scan.
Choose an appropriate window percentage for exclusion of data during respiratory movement, usually 30%.
Press Filter to perform the navigator analysis.
Separate heart navigator from the respiratory navigator.
Set number of CINE frames to 32.
Press sort k-space.
Choose appropriate settings for compressed sensing regularization.
Press reconstruct.
Set wavelet regularization parameter in the spatial dimensions (WVxyz) to 0.001 or 0.
Set total variation constraint in the CINE dimension (TVcine) to 0.1.
Set total variation constraint in the spatial dimension (TVxyz) to 0.
Set total variation constraint in the dynamics dimension (TVdyn) to 0.05.
Preview the CINE movie to evaluate reconstruction quality.
Export DICOM images for further analysis using Export DCM.
Load multi-slice short-axis scan into the plugin for volumetric measurements.
Assign end-systolic (ES) label to the corresponding cardiac frame.
Assign end-diastolic (ED) label to the corresponding cardiac frame.
Segment the endomyocardial borders in the ES and ED frames using contour tools.
Select midventricular short-axis CINE images for diastolic measurement.
Load selected images into the plugin for volumetric measurements.
Assign ED and ES labels to the corresponding cardiac frames.
Use contour tools to segment the endocardial border for all frames.
Ensure smooth transitions of segmentation throughout the cardiac cycle by comparing neighboring frames.
Export time evolution from all cardiac frames and LV endomyocardial volumes (LV ENDO).
Apply a custom-built script to calculate the E'/A' ratio.
Apply Savitzky-Golay filter for robust calculation of dV/dt curves.
Use semi-automatic peak detection to find the E' and A' peaks.
Select 2CH, 3CH, and 4CH long-axis CINE images for strain and HDF calculations.
Load selected images into the plugin for volumetric measurements.
Assign ED and ES labels to corresponding cardiac frames in each slice orientation.
Use contour tools to segment the endocardial border for all frames in all three orientations.
Compare segmentation of neighboring frames to ensure smooth transitions throughout the cardiac cycle.
Run the plugin for strain and HDF analysis after contours are drawn.
Assign acquired datasets to corresponding 2CH, 3CH, and 4CH view labels.
Execute strain analysis on assigned datasets.
Draw mitral valve diameter at end-diastolic frame in all three orientations for HDF analysis.
Draw aorta diameter in the 3-chamber long-axis image for HDF analysis.
